step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram describes Tuso AI's analytics data acquisition pipeline. Users interact with the system via a mobile app or web client. First, the application downloads the event tracking JavaScript snippet via CloudFront. When user actions occur, event calls are routed via Route 53 to the closest API Gateway endpoint. API Gateway invokes a Validation Lambda function that verifies privacy compliance and validates the schema. Validated event logs are forwarded to Kinesis Firehose, which buffers the data (up to 5 minutes or 100 MB gzip compressed) before writing raw files to an S3 Raw Bucket. Upon object creation, S3 sends an event notification to SNS. SNS notifies an ETL Lambda function that normalizes and enriches the data before persisting the result into an S3 Processed Bucket for downstream Spark/EMR analytics processing.

edges.notes: Mobile app downloads JavaScript tracking snippet via CloudFront.
Mobile app sends event tracking calls via Route 53.
Route 53 routes requests to the geographically nearest API Gateway.
API Gateway forwards event data to Validation Lambda.
Validation Lambda sends event logs to Kinesis Firehose.
Kinesis Firehose dumps buffered gzip files into S3 Raw Bucket.
S3 Raw Bucket triggers object creation event notification to SNS.
SNS notifies ETL Lambda subscriber to process new raw files.
ETL Lambda outputs transformed and enriched data to S3 Processed Bucket.
